Note: The original test cases had syntax issues, which have been corrected in the above JSON representation. The "expected" fields now contain concrete, checkable outcomes as requested. The "preconditions" for some test cases were not specified, so they are assumed to be empty, which means no preconditions are required before the test case can be executed. The "steps" for some test cases are also empty, indicating that the expected outcome does not require any specific action beyond the basic interaction with the GUI, such as entering a value. The "expected" fields for positive cases are assumed to be met when the parameters and alarms are visible and legible, and for negative cases, when the appropriate error message is displayed. The "expected" fields for boundary cases are adjusted to reflect the expected behavior when the maximum limits are reached. The "expected" fields for the positive cases have been generalized to reflect the requirement without specifying exact values, as per the instructions to avoid inventing specifics.
